title: Direct multi-model dark-matter search with gravitational-wave interferometers using data from the first part of the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run
extended_summary:
This paper is a physics paper, not an education study. It reports a direct search for ultralight dark matter using gravitational-wave interferometer data from the first part of LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA’s fourth observing run (O4a). The authors investigate three dark-matter candidates: scalar dilatons, vector dark photons, and massive tensor bosons, each of which could induce different measurable strains in the detectors.

The study develops and applies three analysis pipelines to existing interferometer data: a cross-correlation method, a BSD excess-power method, and an LPSD method. These methods are designed to search for narrow-band signals in strain data and then derive upper limits on the relevant coupling strengths in the absence of detections. The paper uses data from the LIGO Hanford and Livingston detectors during O4a; Virgo and KAGRA are mentioned as part of the collaboration, but the analyzed dataset is the U.S.-based LIGO data.

The main conclusion is that none of the searched-for dark-matter signals were detected, but the resulting constraints improve on earlier limits in several cases, including stronger bounds for dilaton and dark-photon couplings and the first interferometer-based constraints on tensor dark matter. Because the paper is about fundamental physics data analysis rather than education, it contains no K-12 population, intervention, or learning outcome relevant to the requested topic.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a physics paper on dark matter searches with gravitational-wave interferometers, not a K-12 education study. It contains no educational intervention, comparator, or student outcome methodology relevant to the requested taxonomy.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no educational impact on K-12 science reasoning, inquiry, or achievement because the paper does not study education at all.
